overall_summary: This lease shifts an unusual amount of risk and cost onto you. Two clauses are likely unenforceable in California even if you sign (the oversized deposit and the repair waiver), and several others are worth negotiating before you commit.

flags.title: Security deposit is three times the legal cap
flags.clause: Tenant shall pay a security deposit equal to three (3) months' rent ($7,200).
flags.why: You would hand over $7,200 up front, and money you overpay is hard to claw back.
flags.law: Cal. Civ. Code §1950.5 (as amended by AB 12, July 1, 2024) caps residential security deposits at one month's rent.
flags.fix: Ask for the deposit to be reduced to one month's rent ($2,400), citing §1950.5.

flags.title: You'd waive your right to a habitable home
flags.clause: Tenant accepts the premises 'as is' and waives all claims relating to habitability, and is responsible for all repairs, including plumbing and heating.
flags.why: Heat, hot water, plumbing and weatherproofing are the landlord's legal job, and you cannot sign that protection away.
flags.law: Cal. Civ. Code §1941.1 (implied warranty of habitability); waivers are void under §1942.1.
flags.fix: Strike the waiver and restore landlord responsibility for structural, plumbing, heating and safety repairs.

flags.title: Late fee is a punitive per-day charge
flags.clause: Rent received after the 3rd incurs a $150 fee plus $25 per additional day.
flags.why: A late fee must roughly match the landlord's actual costs; compounding daily fees are classic unenforceable penalties.
flags.law: California courts void late fees that are not a reasonable estimate of damages (unconscionable penalties).
flags.fix: Ask for a single, modest flat fee (around $50) after a 3-5 day grace period.

flags.title: Landlord can enter with no notice
flags.clause: Landlord may enter the premises at any time to inspect or show the unit.
flags.why: You could lose any expectation of privacy in your own home.
flags.law: Cal. Civ. Code §1954 requires 24-hour written notice, except in emergencies.
flags.fix: Add: entry only on 24-hour written notice, during normal hours, except emergencies.

flags.title: Non-refundable 'cleaning fee' taken from the deposit
flags.clause: A $400 non-refundable cleaning fee will be deducted from the security deposit.
flags.why: California does not allow non-refundable deposit deductions; cleaning can only be charged to return the unit to its move-in condition.
flags.fix: Remove the non-refundable fee; cleaning charges must be itemized against actual condition.

flags.title: Guests cost $50 a night after two nights
flags.clause: Guests staying more than two consecutive nights incur a $50/night charge.
flags.why: Aggressive guest fees are common friction points with roommates and partners.
flags.law: No specific cap, but unreasonable guest restrictions can be challenged as interference with quiet enjoyment.
flags.fix: Ask to raise the free allowance to 5-7 nights per month.

flags.title: No subletting, ever
flags.clause: Subletting or assignment of any kind is prohibited.
flags.why: If you study abroad or leave for a summer internship, you keep paying rent with no options.
flags.law: California allows reasonable consent standards when the lease requires landlord consent; a total ban is enforceable but inflexible.
flags.fix: Ask for subletting with landlord's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.

positives: Rent is fixed for the full 12-month term.
The lease does not require you to waive a jury trial or mandate arbitration.
